title: The 5 Tallest Rockets Ever Flown, Ranked (#1 Beats Saturn V)

scenes.text: The five tallest rockets ever flown, ranked. The one that went to the Moon isn't number one.

scenes.label: SLS · 98 m
scenes.text: Number five: NASA's Space Launch System. About ninety-eight meters tall, the moon rocket of today.

scenes.label: Ares I-X · 100 m
scenes.text: Number four: Ares I-X, a NASA test rocket. About one hundred meters tall, and it flew just once, in two thousand nine.

scenes.label: N1 · 105 m
scenes.text: Number three: the Soviet N1. About one hundred and five meters tall, and all four of its launches failed.

scenes.label: Saturn V · 110 m
scenes.text: Number two: the Saturn V. About one hundred and ten meters, the rocket that took astronauts to the Moon.

scenes.label: Starship · ~120 m
scenes.text: Number one: SpaceX Starship with its Super Heavy booster. About one hundred and twenty meters, taller than the Saturn V.

description:
The five tallest rockets ever flown, ranked by fully stacked height.
From NASA's SLS to SpaceX Starship, which stands taller than the Saturn V that went to the Moon.
Which rocket would you most like to watch launch?
first_comment: Which rocket would you watch launch first? And what should we rank next?
